newsitem.title: TAIWAN: Taiwan to sell down state's United Micro holdings.
newsitem.headline: Taiwan to sell down state's United Micro holdings.

text.p: Taiwan's economics ministry said on Friday it would auction 7.44 million of the state's 145 million shares of United Microelectronics Corp on November 21.
The selldown represents 0.275 percent of all stock in Taiwan's number two semiconductor maker and about five percent of the state's United Micro holdings, a ministry spokesman said.

"We have applied to the Taiwan Stock Exchange on Thursday to sell the 7.44 million state shares of United Microelectronics and we plan to auction them on November 21," a ministry official said by telephone.
"We won't announce the base price for the auction, but the market price should be a good reference," she said.
United Microelectronics ended at T$38.20 on Thursday. In late trade on Friday, it was down 50 cents at T$37.70.
Including the 7.44 million shares, the ministry now holds 145 million, or 5.3 percent, of United Microelectonics shares, the official said.
Brokers said the market would be interested in the auction.

"Investors will be interested in buying the state shares of United Microelectronics because the semiconductor industry's oversupply situation will be over in 1998," said Michael Hung, head of research at Nikko Securities.
"Semiconductor shares are expected to start reflecting the end of the oversupply situation early in the second quarter of 1997," he added.
Hung said the semiconductor industry had bottomed out in July 1996, and was now in a short rebound due to the fourth quarter hot-sale season, although this was likely to change.
"New manufacturing capacity will enter again in 1997, resulting in a new oversupply situation then," he said.
